title: In Abraham's seed all families of the earth will be blessed
summary: God promised that in Abraham's seed all nations would be blessed. Peter (Acts 3:25-26) and Paul (Gal. 3:8, 16) say the seed is Christ, through whom the blessing went first to Israel and then to the Gentiles; it is still spreading.

title: They look and stare upon me
summary: The psalm of the cross says the sufferer could count his bones while people looked and stared at him. At the crucifixion "the people stood beholding" and the soldiers sat down and watched him there.
agreement: commonly cited in evangelical Messianic-prophecy lists

title: "He hath done this": It is finished
summary: Psalm 22 ends by saying a people yet to be born would be told "that he hath done this" (the work is done). Jesus' last word on the cross was "It is finished," and the news has been told to every generation since.
agreement: commonly cited in evangelical Messianic-prophecy lists

title: He will feed His flock like a shepherd
summary: Right after "Behold your God!" Isaiah says the Lord will come and feed His flock like a shepherd, carrying the lambs. Jesus called Himself the Good Shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep, and the apostles call Him the great Shepherd.

title: I have set my face like a flint
summary: The Servant, about to be beaten and spat upon (Isa. 50:6), sets his face like a flint without shame. Knowing what waited for Him there, Jesus "stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem" and walked ahead of His disciples on the way.
agreement: commonly cited in evangelical Messianic-prophecy lists

title: Israel provoked to jealousy by a people that were not a people
summary: Moses foretold that God would move Israel to jealousy with "those which are not a people," and Isaiah that He would be found by a nation that did not seek Him while Israel resisted. Paul quotes both: the Gentiles received the gospel gladly while many in the synagogues were filled with envy.

title: The woman's anointing will be told wherever the gospel is preached

fulfilled.label: 1st century onward (told in Matthew, Mark and John)

summary: Jesus said that wherever the gospel was preached in the whole world, what Mary of Bethany had done would be told as a memorial of her. Three Gospels record it, and it has been told wherever the gospel has gone.

title: Peter's faith will not fail; once turned he will strengthen his brothers
summary: On the night He foretold Peter's denial, Jesus said He had prayed that Peter's faith would not fail and that, once converted, he would strengthen his brothers. After his restoration Peter led the disciples and preached the Pentecost sermon.

title: Adversaries will not be able to answer the wisdom given to you
summary: Jesus told the disciples that when brought before rulers they need not prepare, for He would give them a mouth and wisdom their adversaries could not answer. Before the council the leaders "could say nothing against" Peter and John, and Stephen's opponents "were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake."

title: Signs will follow believers: tongues, healing, serpents
summary: The risen Jesus said believers would cast out devils, speak with new tongues, take up serpents unharmed and heal the sick by laying on hands. Acts records tongues at Pentecost, a spirit cast out at Philippi, and Paul unharmed by a viper and healing the sick on Malta. (Mark 16:9-20 is missing from the two oldest Greek manuscripts but is in the KJV.)

title: Let down your nets: the great catch of fish
summary: After a night of catching nothing, Simon was told to launch out into the deep and let down the nets for a catch. The nets enclosed so many fish that they broke and two boats began to sink.

title: Cast the net on the right side and you will find
summary: After the resurrection, the disciples had fished all night with nothing when Jesus told them to cast the net on the right side of the ship. They could not draw it in for the multitude of fish, 153 large fish, and the net did not break.

title: "Thy son liveth": the nobleman's son healed at a distance

fulfilled.label: c. AD 29 (the same hour, at Capernaum)

summary: At Cana Jesus told a nobleman from Capernaum, "Go thy way; thy son liveth." On his way home his servants met him with the news, and the fever had left the boy at the seventh hour, the very hour Jesus spoke.

title: No man will eat fruit of you hereafter: the fig tree withers
summary: On the way into Jerusalem the day after His entry, Jesus said of a leafy but fruitless fig tree, "No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever." The next morning the disciples saw it dried up from the roots.

title: Of those You gave Me I have lost none

fulfilled.label: night of 9-10 Apr AD 32 (arrest in Gethsemane)

summary: Jesus said none of those the Father gave Him would be lost except the son of perdition. At His arrest He told the soldiers, "let these go their way," and John says this fulfilled His saying: the disciples got away unharmed.

title: Jerusalem will not receive Paul's testimony; he is sent to the Gentiles

given.label: c. AD 37 (Paul's first visit to Jerusalem)

summary: Praying in the Temple, Paul was told to leave Jerusalem quickly because they would not receive his testimony, for he would be sent far off to the Gentiles. The Hellenist Jews tried to kill him and he was sent away to Tarsus. Years later the Jerusalem crowd shouted him down at the word "Gentiles."

title: Peter: the men who buried your husband will carry you out
summary: When Sapphira repeated her husband's lie, Peter said the young men who had buried Ananias were at the door and would carry her out. She fell down at once and they carried her out and buried her beside her husband.

title: Saul sees in a vision Ananias coming to restore his sight

fulfilled.label: c. AD 34 (three days after the Damascus road)

summary: While Saul prayed, blind, in Judas' house on Straight Street, he saw in a vision a man named Ananias coming to lay hands on him so that he would see. Ananias came, laid his hands on him, and the scales fell from his eyes.

title: Cornelius told to send for Peter, lodging with Simon the tanner
prophet: An angel to Cornelius; the Spirit to Peter
summary: An angel told Cornelius to send to Joppa for Simon Peter, lodging with Simon a tanner by the sea; the Spirit then told Peter that three men were looking for him. The messengers found Peter at that very house, and the first Gentile household received the Spirit.

title: Paul: Elymas the sorcerer will be blind for a season
summary: When Elymas tried to turn the proconsul Sergius Paulus from the faith, Paul said he would be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. Mist and darkness fell on him at once and he groped for someone to lead him, and the proconsul believed.

title: In Corinth no man will set on Paul to hurt him
summary: In a night vision the Lord told Paul not to be afraid, for no one would attack him to hurt him and He had many people in Corinth. Paul stayed eighteen months, and when the Jews brought him before the proconsul Gallio the case was thrown out before Paul even spoke.

title: Paul: after I leave, grievous wolves will enter the Ephesian flock
summary: Paul warned the Ephesian elders that after his departure wolves would come in and men from among them would rise speaking perverse things. His letters to Timothy at Ephesus name Hymenaeus, Alexander and Philetus and say all in Asia had turned from him, and Christ's letter to Ephesus praises them for testing false apostles.

title: "Say to the north, Give up": the return from the north country

fulfilled.label: 1989–2000s (about a million from the former USSR)

fulfilment: Emigration of Soviet and post-Soviet Jews to Israel, opened from 1989
summary: Isaiah heard God say to the north, "Give up," and Jeremiah saw a great company, including the blind, the lame and women with child, return from the north country. After decades of refused exit visas, the Soviet Union opened its gates in 1989 and about a million Jews came to Israel over the following years.
agreement: commonly cited by evangelical prophecy teachers

title: Vines planted again on the mountains of Samaria
fulfilment: Jewish vineyards and wineries in the hills of Samaria since the 1970s
summary: Jeremiah foretold that Israel would again plant vines on the mountains of Samaria and eat the fruit as ordinary food. After the hills of Samaria came under Israeli control in 1967, Jewish farmers planted vineyards there that now produce wine commercially.
agreement: commonly cited by evangelical prophecy teachers

title: Old people and children playing will fill Jerusalem's streets
fulfilment: Jerusalem resettled by Jews gathered from east and west, from 1948 and after 1967
summary: Zechariah foresaw old men and women with staffs sitting in Jerusalem's streets and the streets full of boys and girls playing, as God gathers His people from the east and the west. A small first fulfilment came after the Babylonian exile; prophecy teachers point to today's rebuilt Jerusalem of Jews from every land.
agreement: commonly cited by evangelical prophecy teachers
